source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Judges 1–5 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 145 original source records are bound exactly once.

key_decisions.decision: Name the mutilation directly and preserve the sequence of pursuit, capture and injury.
Keep seventy, the table image and mutilation, attributing the explanation of divine repayment to the speaker.
Retain the conquest claim here alongside the continued Jebusite residence later in the chapter.
Keep the younger-brother relationship with its ambiguous attachment, explained in a note.
Make the implied Othniel explicit while preserving Achsah’s agency and the definite field in this version.
Preserve unnamed Kenite kinship, all locations and the unspecific people without harmonizing another account.
Retain reciprocal help, the destruction and the resulting name linked to devotion.
Keep all three capture claims and repeated territory without reconciling the next verse.
Make Judah the human agent while retaining the divine presence and the inability attributed to iron chariots.
Retain Benjamin rather than substituting Judah from Joshua 15:63 and keep continued residence.
Keep the killing beside the explicit exception for the man’s entire kin group.
Retain all five places in this order, each dependent-town group and the Canaanites’ determination.
Keep the distinction between coercive labor and expulsion; do not present accommodation as equality.
Retain the reversal: Israelites live among Canaanites, not the other way around.
Preserve the residence relationship and repeat both towns in the labor clause.
Keep the Amorites as effective agents and Dan’s restricted movement.
Preserve all places, the heavy-hand image and coerced labor.
Keep the Amorite label and both starting references, with Sela’s possible rock sense noted.
